tb21_profile.skill: Read code off a raster image (vision or tesseract OCR), reconstruct the pseudocode exactly including loop bounds and operator details, then execute its semantics faithfully to produce one exact final value
tb21_profile.domain: OCR / image-to-text on a code screenshot, plus small-program semantics and hex-digest arithmetic; no library stack in particular
tb21_profile.task_form: reverse-engineer-a-spec-from-an-artifact then implement-from-spec, graded on a single exact string in /app/output.txt

verifier_notes: No grade I checked looked wrong for this task. Three of the TerminalWorld picks (tw_102792, tw_318029, tw_352867) are FREE and their grades look right: each is satisfied by producing a non-empty file or a valid-looking artifact, so none of them entered final_top10. task_000079_76a46e77 and task_000060_fb4491c0 in TMax are `behavioral` (exit-status only) which is why stronger-graded siblings from the same OCR family outrank them.

notes: This is a two-halves task (read the image, then execute the snippet) and the pools split on it. CalibForge has a whole games_* family of read-a-rendered-board-then-compute tasks plus one literal code-from-screenshot task, and it wins outright. TMax-15K has an equally strong OCR-spec family (task_0000xx through task_0001xx are all 'extract a constant or a rule from a PNG then implement it'), which retrieval only partially surfaced - task_005252_9cc400a9 and task_004606_391aae46 were in the shortlist but the OCR cluster around task_000105/000108/000117 had to be found by searching for 'tesseract'. Terminal-Lego contributes exactly one strong candidate (task_09114, implement-from-pseudocode-literally) and three thin OCR ones; ranks 6-10 there are filler. TerminalWorld and Recursive-Task-Synthesis have no image-reading tasks at all - `tools.py search tw/rts` for OCR/tesseract/screenshot returns nothing relevant - so both lists are honest adjacency picks (exact-digest computation, follow-a-hidden-spec) and none scores above 3. SWE-Smith's pdfplumber cluster is a genuinely useful surprise: glyph clustering and layout-preserving extraction is the algorithmic core of reading text off a page, and retrieval surfaced none of it.
